g.text: America's electro-industrial trade deficit sits in a few
In January-August 2026 the US imported $193bn of clean-energy and grid goods and exported $76bn
(2.5 to 1). Imports are largest in electric vehicles, grid and solar; relative to exports they
are highest in batteries (3.5 to 1) and nuclear (3.2 to 1). 55% of clean-energy and grid imports
are assembled goods and 27% components; the US is a net exporter of fuels and of raw materials.

g.text: B. Imports and exports by supply-chain stage, January-August 2026
Technology totals are attributed: a product in several technologies (static converters, switchgear, cable) counts in each, so
technology rows overlap; stage totals count each HS6 product once (split equally where it sits in different stages) and exclude
Deployment, which repeats Assembly. Net balance (bold) = exports - imports. Geothermal and green hydrogen have no defensible traded
All technologies together: imports $358bn (-0.1% vs January-August 2024), exports $360bn (+19.7%). A trade deficit is not by itself a
Sources: US Census Bureau imports for consumption by HTS-10 line and partner (via the Trade War Tracker); US exports by HS6 (Census
data as reported to UN Comtrade); NEIS electro-industrial HS6 basket (data/reference/energy_hs6_master.csv).
